The applied plan has 0 runs above the single-run ceiling (R7C-FREEZE-3: 60 stale cells, up to 28 minutes above), no step a short run did not earn, and no race touch or taper quality the direct answer lacks (R7C-FREEZE-3: 16). Clinical-first and C11 are unchanged.

Not READY, for three reasons. (1) P7-F03: a report recorded without the first-recorded clock (a record written before R7C-FREEZE-4, or a clock lost) keeps R7C-FREEZE-3's reading; 23 of 200 legacy cells stay stale and VALID after clearance (shortened, all-adverse and alternating mixed answers; up to LONG 65 where the record allows 41; a taper quality session). (2) P7-F02: Phase 7 widens the QE-R7C-12 class: after a direct shortened answer a later decision of the answer week raises the following week's VALID easy runs above R7C-FREEZE-3 and above the week's own review (GEN b=5: 41/41 to 45/45), until that review; the handoff says the opposite. Covered by C9's consumer part, extended to every answer. (3) The consumer conditions C2, C3, C8, C9 and C11, and C9's Engineering part on the handler re-compositions, are obligations no frozen byte discharges.

P7-F02 is not escalated to a blocker: it is the QE-R7C-12 class Engineering classified MINOR, it touches only the following week's conditional projection (never the answer week, quality or race), stays within the projection's single-run ceiling, is replaced by the week's own review or the first decision of the next week, and in the measured cell C9's consumer part already applies literally (the day-2 answer left day 0's run elapsed). conditions.text: While a result has planValidity REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION (a pending UNREPORTED_TRAINING question, a HOLD such as R4, or a clinical dependency), no consumer presents the stored run doses ahead as a prescription. The question, and any strength change kept beside it, are the only actionable items. Carry this in the freeze record and the handoff.

conditions.text: The answer path is low-friction and factual: done or not done per session, or a declared break with its reason, screened clinically. HealthKit evidence is used before asking where available. Non-response never falls back silently to credit or zero. While referenceState.pending.signal is present, the answer is delivered as a plain review of that week or as the pending event kind with its signals. An answer inside another event kind is followed by the held signal re-submitted before the plan is presented. A RECOVERED event does not carry the answer (it stays ASK). An answer to UNREPORTED_TRAINING that a decision recorded without applying it (a refusal such as the R4 HOLD; a handler clinical route: a substitution with pain or a clinical return report; an ASK whose proposal the client did not apply under C2) is applied by the first eligible decision after it, with no re-send, as the same answer delivered directly, and after a clinical route only after qualified clearance, which the runtime cannot give. On R7C-FREEZE-4 this holds for every answer shape measured: known stops, runs done in full, runs done shorter than prescribed (at 60 % or 80 %, the long run only, with the other runs not done), adverse responses, mixed answers and their combinations; re-sending such an answer changes nothing. An eligibility clinical flag returns before any report is read and records nothing, so after qualified clearance its answer is re-sent or asked again (R5). A correction of an earlier report is different: one that a decision recorded without applying it (measured: a clinical substitution, then cleared) is applied only by the week's own review, re-send included, and until then the plan built from the uncorrected report stays VALID; so after such a decision the run doses remaining in that week are not presented as a prescription until that review. This rests on the record: whether an earlier review read a run report is taken from the clock at which the completed-work record first held it (provenance.firstRecordedAt, written only by the runtime), never from the gate that review gave. Consumers carry the record exactly as the runtime returns it, send new reports only as observations, and never add rows of their own or drop, set or rewrite that clock. A report without it (a record written before R7C-FREEZE-4, a row a client built itself, or a clock lost) is read as on R7C-FREEZE-3, and any answer recorded that way can stay unapplied after clearance, re-send included, with the stored doses VALID: runs done short, adverse or mixed, and also runs done in full or adverse when a week of the window was closed by a decision that records no gates, such as a nonclinical exercise substitution (measured: a long run of 65 minutes where the record allows 41; QUALITY 34 / LONG 60 where an all-adverse answer plans EASY 25 / LONG 35; a taper quality session and a race touch where the direct answer plans easy running). No such record is carried into any use beyond the offline reference; if one is, after a decision that recorded an answer on it without applying it, the run doses remaining in that week are not presented as a prescription: the qualified human's clearance and the week's own review decide, and that review re-plans the following week from the facts. Cadence and wording belong to G03.
The internal label MISSED for an elapsed session with no report never surfaces as "not done"; history and adherence keep "no report" distinct from "reported not done".
Apply a nonclinical substitution strength-only while the run question is pending. Next runtime revision; not blocking.

conditions.text: The closure records as disclosed residuals: D1. B2. B1. The ratified fifth fixture. R1: fixed on the factual re-plan route; persisting on handler routes that re-compose the weeks from the answer week (a nonclinical EXERCISE_SUBSTITUTION, a short RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE, an EVENT_DATE_CHANGE): week b+1 stored up to EASY 50/QUALITY 34/LONG 60, and a 25-minute race touch in race week after a taper answer, until the first decision of the next week, which in every measured case asks or re-plans within the single-run ceiling; unchanged on R7C-FREEZE-4, where the non-handler one-step differences at the first decision of week b+1 are now 0 (16 on R7C-FREEZE-3). R2 with A* as the only differing reference (the one-step differences at the first decision of week b+1 belong here). R3 persisting one step into the following week; on the answer path the held long run can sit up to 10 minutes above the on-time step-back (GEN b=5, gap from week 2: LONG 65 against 55), identical on R7C-FREEZE-2; with every run adverse the answer path holds the easy and long runs one step (5 minutes) above the same facts read by the review before the answer week (for example EASY 25 / LONG 45 against 20 / 40), still below the stored plan and the executed answer's plan (E1 holds); identical on R7C-FREEZE-3. R4: A SCHEDULE_CHANGE in the program's last week throws and returns HOLD, and the HOLD remains (Engineering). An answer it records is applied by the next decision as delivered directly: a known stop by the ceiling re-plan; runs done in full, shorter than prescribed, adverse or mixed by the recorded-answer re-plan (no residual measured). On a record without first-recorded clocks, see C3. R5: An eligibility clinical flag returns before the reports are read and records nothing, so the answer is re-sent or asked again after qualified clearance (C3). A handler clinical route records the answer, and nothing is prescribed while it stands. After qualified clearance the first eligible decision applies it with no re-send for every answer shape measured on R7C-FREEZE-4 (known stops; runs done in full, shorter than prescribed, adverse or mixed, P6-F01's patterns included), and re-sending changes nothing. On a record whose answer rows carry no first-recorded clock, any answer such a route recorded can keep R7C-FREEZE-3's reading (C3, QE-R7C-15). SSCTR-SD5-02, narrowed (a held signal survives a change kept beside the question; it is still dropped by an answer inside a non-review kind that returns VALID). QE-R7C-05. Never reported, easy running: within the intake window a credited progression below the single-run ceiling, quality activation included, stands at non-review decisions until the week's own review (e.g. EASY 50/QUALITY 34/LONG 65 against the reviewed EASY 45/45/LONG 60). Never reported, restart or walk/jog: outside the unknown window by design; the restart ladder progresses on credit (EASY 20 to EASY 30/LONG 35 by week 5, against 15 on the reviewed path and the entry ceiling on the record) until the week's own review. The reach of the recorded-answer re-plan (R7C-FREEZE-3): a stored plan resting on projection over its run window follows the record at the first decision whose factual plan differs, never above R7C-FREEZE-2 or the single-run ceiling in any measured cell, and overperformance is not adopted outside a review; where weeks were never reviewed, the facts reading holds every run role (no step): after adverse long-run responses the long run stays at the stored dose where the weekly review would step it back (up to 10 minutes above the reviewed path), and a lift also executed in another session of the week keeps its executed load where the review holds it (24 against 22 kg); with an earlier evidence anchor in the window the projection still stands until the week's own review (Property B: the Saturday-only lift 24 kg against 22 kg in history); on the timely path, see C11; since R7C-FREEZE-4 the reports a review did not read are decided per report from the clock at which the record first held them, so late reports of runs done short or adverse count as unread, as late full-dose reports do. QE-R7C-12: see C9 (r6). QE-R7C-15: on a record without first-recorded clocks the R7C-FREEZE-3 reading also leaves full-dose and adverse answers unapplied when a week of the window was closed by a decision that records no gates (a nonclinical exercise substitution, a schedule change): 128 of 224 Engineering cells and 13 of 24 SSCTR cells stale and VALID; with clocks all converge (C3). QE-R7C-16: see C11 (b). QE-R7C-18 (pre-existing since R7B2-FREEZE-1, not R7-C): a correction of an on-time report that a clinical route recorded is applied only at the week's own review, re-send included; meanwhile the plan built from the uncorrected report stays VALID (measured: quality one ladder rung ahead, 3x8 against 5x5, and the following week's easy run 55 against 50); consumer guard in C3; the engine fix belongs to a later runtime mission. QE-R7C-14: On R7C-FREEZE-3 the directed tests used full-dose answers only, and the Engineering review recorded three surviving mutants of answeredOnRecord's guards: J-M2 (REGRESS not counted as executed; witnessed), J-M3 (the return-report exclusion removed) and J-M5 (the return-replaced start ignored), the last two not witnessed. Phase 7's directed tests cover shortened, all-adverse and mixed answers, timely reviews that gave HOLD or REGRESS on reports they had, and present and late reports of one week; each Phase 7 mutant (F7-M1..M11) is killed by its own witness, and J-M2 survives only in the reading kept for records without clocks, as F7-M7, killed by the backward-behaviour test. Phase 7 names neither J-M3 nor J-M5; both guards are present in R7C-FREEZE-4, and whether a test now kills them is for the Engineering gate. Corrections recorded by the closure (the freeze record itself is not edited): the backward-behaviour statement 'sound for full-dose and adverse answers; a shortened late answer on such a record reads as on R7C-FREEZE-3' is replaced by C3's legacy clause (any answer can keep the old reading: shortened, adverse and mixed answers, and full-dose and adverse ones where a week of the window was closed by a decision that records no gates; QE-R7C-15); the handoff's QE-R7C-12 sentence 'no dose raised above the plan before or above R7C-FREEZE-3' is replaced by C9 (r6); the differential's 'habitual late reporters (full dose and shortened) included' holds only for its timeline of two decisions a week (QE-R7C-16, C11).

Engine, in the next runtime revision: a held reactive signal is never cleared without being re-evaluated. Any decision that answers the question either re-evaluates it, or keeps it pending with the plan REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION until the signal kind is re-submitted, or at least discloses it. Until then, the consumer obligation in C3 applies.

conditions.text: r2 text: This applies after an answer to UNREPORTED_TRAINING that leaves sessions of the answer week elapsed before it, including the taper-to-race-week case. The following week's conditional projection is not presented or delivered as a prescription until a decision re-plans it: the answer week's review, or the first decision of the next week. The client triggers that decision at the week boundary. Carry this in the freeze record and the handoff, as C2 is carried. Engineering, before any use beyond the offline reference: re-project later weeks without crediting those elapsed unreported sessions (read them as unknown), or mark the projection as conditional on the week's review. Add a directed test that pins week b+1 after a day-2 known-stop answer. Plus the r4 and r5 status notes as carried. Plus (r6): R7C-FREEZE-4 does not change the handler re-compositions (my CC3 re-run: EXERCISE_SUBSTITUTION 44, RETURN_SHORT 14, EVENT_DATE_CHANGE 8, identical to R7C-FREEZE-3; the non-handler one-step differences fall from 16 to 0). The Engineering part is still owed for those routes. QE-R7C-12 (routed to the SSCTR): after an answer delivered directly, a later decision of the answer week can re-plan the following week again with more elapsed run sessions uncredited, and that VALID conditional projection can sit above what the week's own review then plans, by one single-run step on easy runs or one quality rung (a known stop: EASY 20/20 against 15/15; since R7C-FREEZE-4 also after a shortened answer: GEN EASY 45/45 against 41/41, where R7C-FREEZE-3 kept 41/41), never in the answer week, never as a race touch, until the week's review or the first decision of the next week. The consumer part therefore applies after every answer to UNREPORTED_TRAINING, delivered directly or recorded, whether or not a session of the answer week had elapsed before it: the following week's plan is provisional and is not presented or delivered as a prescription until the answer week's review or the first decision of the next week (and C11 for every week after the current one, QE-R7C-16 included). Engineering, a later runtime mission (not blocking), for QE-R7C-12 and QE-R7C-16 alike: a later decision never plans a later week above what the same facts give with the elapsed sessions credited (unknown never plans more than known), or the projection is disclosed as conditional.

conditions.text: Later weeks are provisional. The run doses of any week after the current one are a conditional projection: consumers present them as provisional, never as a prescription, until the decision that closes the week before them (that week's own review, or the first decision of the following week when the review does not happen) has re-planned them, and a change a decision makes to them before then is not surfaced as a coaching change; cadence and wording belong to G03. Measured on R7C-FREEZE-4: (a) on the timely, weekly-reviewed path (since R7C-FREEZE-3, unchanged), a decision made before the week's review while a run session of the week has elapsed with no report re-plans the following week without crediting it: it holds the quality step (GEN THRESHOLD 3x10 back to the week's 4x8; R10K 5x4 back to 6x3; taper 3x4 to 3x3), and the week's review restores the progression once the reports arrive (24 of 210 measured cells change mid-week, 0 after the review); (b) for a habitual late reporter whose runs are done short, the runs of each week reported after that week's review (QE-R7C-16, since R7C-FREEZE-4), a decision before the week's review re-plans later weeks from the facts, mostly down (quality to easy running, taper easy runs 30 to 15, a race-week race touch to easy running) but with same-role raises of 3 to 5 minutes up to six weeks ahead (EASY 41 to 45, 46 to 50, 30 to 35; LONG 62 to 65, 67 to 70, 40 to 45: 16 raises in 19 re-plans, 14 above what the week's own review then plans), VALID until that review, never in the current week, while the executed weeks stay identical to R7C-FREEZE-3 and never above the timely path; (c) after an answer to UNREPORTED_TRAINING, see C9 (QE-R7C-12). This is the accepted unknown semantics, not a new dose.

queryLog.result: Access works. No 2025-2026 systematic review surfaced. A 2025 BJSM cohort (Frandsen et al.) associating single-run spikes relative to the longest run of the prior 30 days with injury hazard, and the 2018 Damsted et al. systematic review (very limited evidence on load changes) appeared as search snippets only; neither full text was read and neither is relied on. Negative screen, standard mode, limited.

aeReview.q4_changeNecessary: Yes, against the same answer delivered directly as comparator; the recorded path now equals it in every measured cell.

items.classification: ACCEPTED_UNDER_PRESENTATION_RULE (C11 replaced so that it covers it literally); engine item kept with QE-R7C-12 for a later runtime mission, not blocking
reason: Reproduced independently (p7-late-short-reporter: GEN and R10K, runs at 60 % and 80 %, strength on its day, weekly review on day 6, runs reported on day 1 of the next week): 19 recorded re-plans on R7C-FREEZE-4 where R7C-FREEZE-3 keeps; 16 same-role raises of at most 5 minutes; 14 above what the week's own review then plans; 0 in the current week; executed weeks identical to R7C-FREEZE-3 in all four timelines.

It is the QE-R7C-12 / P7-F02 mechanism (the week's elapsed unreported runs uncredited, the dose then taken from the projection's single-run ceiling), reached for a reporter class R7C-FREEZE-3 did not reach. The raises sit in conditional weeks only and rest on the projection crediting the current week's sessions still ahead: 13 of 16 are above the ceiling the record allows at that moment (EASY 45 against 41; LONG 65 and 70 against 57), as R7C-FREEZE-3's own projection already was for those long runs (62 and 67 against 57).

For a habitual 60 % runner such a raise is not a step the record earned, so it must never be a prescription. But it lasts two days, the week's own review replaces it before any of those weeks starts, and nothing executed changes, so it is not a blocker: the presentation rule covers it. C9's r6 note and the r5 C11 did not literally cover it (no UNREPORTED_TRAINING answer; not the timely path), so C11 is replaced by a rule for every week after the current one, and C9's engine item names QE-R7C-16.

Reproduced independently (p7-gateless-closer: GEN b=7 and R10K taper, gap from week 0 or 2, a gap week closed at day 6 by a nonclinical substitution or a schedule change, a clinical substitution carrying the answer, cleared): with clocks 0 of 24 cells differ from the direct answer; with every clock removed 13 of 24 stay stale and VALID, including full-dose (GEN g=2: QUALITY 34 where the answer plans 43, here more conservative) and adverse answers (GEN g=0: QUALITY 34 / LONG 60 where it plans EASY 25 / LONG 35; R10K taper g=0: QUALITY 25 / LONG 40 and a race touch where it plans EASY 15 throughout).

The first r6 C3 already bound consumers for any answer on a record without clocks, but its list of affected shapes read as exhaustive and was wrong. The replacement widens that sentence to any answer, names the gate-less closer, adds rows a client builds itself (which carry no clock), and requires new reports to go in only as observations.

items.classification: C3_WORDS_IT_NOW (consumer guard), plus a C7 disclosure; engine fix routed to a later runtime mission
reason: From the Engineering output (p7-x3b, not re-run): a correction of week 5's on-time long run to 60 %, recorded by a clinical substitution and cleared, re-sent or not, leaves QUALITY 43 (3x8) / LONG 75 / next week EASY 55 VALID where the correction delivered directly plans QUALITY 48 (5x5, the lower rung) / LONG 75 / EASY 50, until the week's own review, which converges.

The measured magnitude is one ladder rung and 5 minutes, within the ceiling. But only one shape was measured, and the first r6 C3 says a recorded answer is applied with no re-send, which a consumer could read as covering corrections. A disclosure alone would leave that reading open, so C3 states the difference and the same guard as for records without clocks: after a decision that recorded a correction without applying it, the run doses remaining in that week are not presented as a prescription until that week's own review. No clinical judgment is involved; clearance stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED.
